title: Deployment platform: repository, deploy, secrets, migrations, monitoring
description:
Split out of epic-8ebe64173d934f72a339c32bc2eaaf7d ("Create product production") on 2026-09-05 by architect-b63fabf3, with the human's authorisation, when that epic measured 101 non-archived rows against the 40 advisory ceiling. This epic holds everything that takes a goal's landed code and makes it RUN somewhere: the repository it lives in, the container it ships as, the secrets it needs, the schema it migrates, and the watch kept on it afterwards.

Five capability bands, in build order: Repository bootstrapping (order 80-83), Containerized deployment (90-93), Secrets and environment (100-103), Database migrations (110-113), Monitoring/backup/rollback (120-123).

STATE AT THE SPLIT: 23 rows, 22 of them live and only ONE done - this is the least-started third of the board and the one with the most headroom to be re-sliced before work begins.
architectureNotes:
BUILD ORDER IS A REAL CONSTRAINT HERE, not paperwork. The scaffold (band 80) decides what the image builds (90), what variables it needs (100), and what migration tool ships in it (110); monitoring (120) probes what deploy produced. A row planned out of that order either invents a contract its producer has not written or re-implements one that exists. Measure the edge before planning a consumer.

TWO SHARED SEAMS TO WATCH, both of which have already bitten the sibling epic:

1. `environment.set_variable` / `environment.unset_variable` (task-a2409cba, task-b3888068, task-d0d1cb5c) publish command kinds through the same shared runtime roster and the same four contract digest mirrors as the operator-gates epic's preview/release/design kinds. Those rows now live in a DIFFERENT epic, so get_context.epicSiblings will NOT surface them: any row here touching runtime-vocabulary.ts must re-census the mirrors itself with a full-tree grep and must run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. This is the one real cost of the split and it is why the rail below exists.

2. Secrets never surface in plaintext (task-d0c63cd8, DONE and kept visible for its live dependents). Every screen, log line, receipt and error path in bands 100-103 inherits that.

EPIC-FINAL: no single integration-and-hardening row lives here. The band parents (task-5ef1a0a9, task-5d309484, task-9ae492b3, task-8f86e105, task-7683a432) are integration-shaped for their own bands, and the whole-product proof stays on task-161b7e9d in the parent epic, which declares dependsOn against all five. Decide deliberately whether to add one here.
epicRails: THE SHARED RUNTIME ROSTER IS OWNED BY A DIFFERENT EPIC NOW. Any row here that adds a command kind must re-census the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors itself with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types, and must run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` - two mirrors live under apps/control-room and are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` and the daemon leg. epicSiblings will not show you the preview/release/design rows that hold the precedent.

PLAN IN BUILD ORDER: scaffold, then image, then variables, then migrations, then monitoring. Before planning a consumer, measure its producer's edge on disk - a declared dependency that does not exist yet is a prerequisite row, never a narrowed DoD or a mock-backed journey.
A SECRET NEVER SURFACES IN PLAINTEXT - not on a screen, not in a log line, not in a receipt, not in an error path, not in a test fixture committed to the tree.

ANYTHING THIS EPIC STARTS, IT STOPS. A deploy, a disposable database, a probe schedule and a backup job each own their teardown on EVERY exit path, including the failure ones. A test that leaks a container or a port makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.
